To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) PDGF is a potent mitogen, chemotactic factor and inducer of cell motility, 2) high concentrations of PDGF were detected in neoplastic cystic brain lesions, 3) PDGF could also been detected in non-neoplastic, cystic brain lesions.
PDGF is found in neoplastic cyst fluids in concentrations that may have a pathogenetic role.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biological significance of the PDGF system in brain tumour growth.
the biological role and clinical significance of PDGF in human brain tumours.
the development of new methods for diagnosis and treatment of malignant tumors, in particular gliomas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PDGF is present at a high concentration in cyst fluids from a variety of neoplastic and also non-neoplastic central nervous system lesions.
PDGF is a growth factor which is present in the brain in vivo and which is produced locally in neoplastic as well as non-neoplastic conditions.
PDGF is a growth factor which may be involved in tumour growth and progression in the brain, but that its role in the pathogenesis and progression of the tumours is not yet known.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PDGF may be involved in the pathophysiology of neoplastic as well as non-neoplastic CNS lesions.
the PDGF concentration is high in neoplastic brain lesions and that the PDGF is locally produced rather that being derived from platelets.
PDGF is a growth factor for astrocytomas in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PDGF is a potential target for cancer therapy.
PDGF may be an important factor for tumour growth in vivo.
we can use the PDGF as a marker for the detection of neoplasms.
